chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the woman who does not menstruate except every three years or more than that.
He said, he said: [She observes] the same number of menstrual periods as she used to menstruate when she was regular, and she must count three menstrual periods, then she may marry if she wishes.

key_terms.اسْتِقَامَتِهَا: Her regularity/consistency (referring to normal menstrual cycle)

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (iddah) for a woman with irregular menstruation who only bleeds every few years?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records Imam al-Sadiq’s ruling for women with prolonged menstrual intervals (istihadha), establishing that their waiting period (iddah) is determined by counting three actual menstrual flows rather than a fixed time duration. This principle highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on physiological reality over arbitrary timeframes, ensuring the woman’s purity status is accurately assessed before remarriage.
